content.title: RULES EVERY NEW PARENT SHOULD FOLLOW FOR THE FIRST YEAR
facts: **Nap when the baby naps** – skipping sleep for chores wrecks your recovery and mood faster than a messy kitchen ever will.
**Batch cook on Sundays** – freeze 4-5 meals in single portions so exhaustion never means skipping a real meal.
**Keep a water bottle by the feeding chair** – breastfeeding and late nights drain fluids fast, sip every time you sit down.
**Accept the first 2 offers of help** – let someone bring food or hold the baby, isolation slows healing and raises stress hormones.
**Step outside for 10 minutes daily** – fresh air resets your nervous system even on zero hours of sleep.
**Lower the bar on day 1** – showered and fed is a successful day, not a failed one.
**Check in with your own doctor at 6 weeks, not just the baby's** – postpartum checkups catch issues parents often brush off.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
The first months with a new baby are brutal on your body, so a few small swaps matter more than people admit. Napping when the baby naps isn't lazy, it's how your body gets back into deep sleep cycles that actual rest (not just lying down) requires to repair tissue and regulate hormones. Batch cooking on a calmer day means on the hard days you're not running on coffee and crackers, which keeps blood sugar steady and mood more stable. And that water bottle by the feeding chair matters more than it sounds, dehydration during feeding windows can worsen fatigue and even milk supply. Everyone's recovery looks different, listen to your own body first.
